items.title: Sonny Rollins — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: it wasn’t Ella Fitzgerald singing, or...you know, it wasn’t a big band uh–Duke Ellington playing some beautiful–no, it was saxophone solo.

ctx.x: What does that mean exactly, “the man?”
Well, it meant that he was the epitome of the saxophone. That Body and Soul had just come out, and Body and Soul you could hear on any street corner in Harlem,

from any uh bar on the jukebox–Body and Soul. See, and Body and Soul was saxophone-played. It wasn’t Ella Fitzgerald singing, or...you know, it wasn’t a big band uh–Duke Ellington playing some beautiful–no, it was saxophone solo. And uh, [Thelonious] Monk used to ask Coleman Hawkins, “Man, how did you make a hit with, with Body and Soul, and you didn’t play the melody? How did that, you know, you never played the melody, and you did all this stuff.” So, it was, it was miraculous what he did with this.
